sectors.name: Renewables & Climate-Tech
themes: Indonesia's mandated 35% renewable energy mix by 2025 and local content rules (TKDN) create durable demand for domestic solar and wind project developers like BRPT and LAPD.
Global cost declines in solar PV and battery storage, combined with Indonesia's nickel-based battery supply chain, structurally lower deployment costs for climate-tech solutions.
Government's accelerated coal phase-down and carbon tax implementation (starting 2025) provide regulatory tailwinds for renewable energy certificates and carbon credit markets.
sectors.ai: Indonesia's renewables sector shows a mixed signal with a slight aggregate decline, but select movers like CSAP and ENPH gaining over 3.5% suggest selective momentum. Focus on domestic players like BRPT and LAPD, which posted gains, as they benefit from Indonesia's push for energy transition and local content requirements. Watch for policy catalysts from the upcoming national energy plan revision.

Government support for domestic food production and halal certification requirements create durable moats for local FMCG players, reducing import competition and supporting pricing power.
Structural underpenetration of modern retail in outer islands provides long-term volume growth runway for companies with strong logistics networks, particularly in snacks and beverages.
sectors.ai: Indonesia consumer/FMCG shows selective strength with coffee (KOPI) and packaged food (AISA, AGAR) surging 25-31% on domestic demand recovery and Eid-related restocking; US-listed peers' +2.25% confirms global softness. Watch for margin compression from rising input costs and potential rate hold by BI. Recommend tactical longs in KOPI and AISA, but avoid broader sector exposure until Q2 earnings confirm sustainability.
